maya: Heads-up — noticed a ~40ms jump in p99 for /v1/generate on the latency dashboard right after the routing policy tweak at ~1741267800. p50/p95 unchanged. :thinking:
jon: Hmm can you drop the dashboard link + sample counts? Could be low-sample artifact. :eyes:
maya: link: https://console.internal/redwood/latency?endpoint=/v1/generate&range=1h
maya: Sample counts look steady (~1800/min), not tiny. p99 moved from ~210ms -> ~255ms around the policy change. p95 ~ unchanged (88ms -> 92ms).
sara: deploy-bot shows: "applied routing-weight-update canary -> 0.25, stable -> 0.75" at 1741267793. Might line up.
deploy-bot: Routing policy update: service=gateway route=/v1/generate old_weights={a:0.8,b:0.2} new_weights={a:0.75,b:0.25} by @sara @ops on 2024-09-14T15:16:33Z
lee: Could be population shift — if variant B has heavier tail (longer KV-cache misses), small weight bump can shift p99 without affecting p95. Have we compared per-variant percentiles?
maya: Good call. Ran a quick split: variant A p99=220ms, variant B p99=420ms (but variant B only ~18% pre-change). After change variant B proportion ~25% and p99 floor moved up.
jon: That explains it. Two questions: 1) do we want routing policy to respect tail-cost (not just average latency)? 2) should console surface per-variant percentiles by default so this is obvious?
sara: 1) We currently optimize weights for throughput & 95th. We don't have an automated tail-aware optimizer. 2) Agree — console default shows merged percentiles which hides this. Maybe add an annotation + easy split-by-(variant|region|client_tag).
lee: Short term: rollback or pin weight for that customer cohort. Long term: add a routing cost function that penalizes p99 when route targets SLAs.
maya: For rollback — can we flip canary back to 0.2? Ops, is that low friction?
ops-bot: @sara you have permission to modify weights. Use `./tools/routing update --service gateway --route /v1/generate --weights a=0.8,b=0.2` to revert. Will require 30s to propagate.
sara: I can revert now unless folks object.
jon: Revert for now, and let's track p99 for 30m. Also file a follow-up: add per-variant pctl to console + a routing policy flag for tail-sensitivity.
maya: Reverted. p99 back down within 2 mins. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
lee: Filing a proposal PR for tail-aware routing logic + console UX mockups. Assigning to eng-platform + eng-runtime for triage.
maya: Added test notes: small weight shifts can move tail a lot if variants have skewed heavy-tail subpopulations. We should add synthetic load tests that exercise tail behavior.
jon: Also add an alert rule: if p99 changes > 15% but p95 < 5% change, annotate recent routing changes in the alert to avoid noisy pager.
sara: Good idea. I'll add an alert runbook entry.
maya: Closing the thread — keeping as a short postmortem in the rollout doc. Thanks!
